text:
On the morning of 14 March 2025, the car park outside Peverell Semiconductors' main campus filled more slowly than usual. Inside, word was already moving between desks that something had been decided.

By afternoon it was official. Peverell laid off 1,200 staff, about 18 percent of its 6,700-person global workforce. Chief Executive Officer Marguerite Oyelaran-Finch confirmed the cuts, which the company set out in a Form 8-K restructuring filing submitted that same day.

She discussed the decision on an investor call, speaking in the measured language that restructurings tend to produce. Chip makers have long lived by cycles of expansion and contraction, hiring in bursts and retrenching in others. Each downturn leaves behind its own roll of departed engineers and technicians. This one, for those who worked at Peverell, now has a number attached.
